sections.h2: Choosing a sale route in Longview
sections.html:
Short on time, you have three choices: hire an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer from someone who will do the repairs. A listing reaches the most buyers. Cash closes faster when repairs, liens, tenants or an estate are complicating things.

Longview is the seat of Gregg County, along Interstate 20 and U.S. highways 80 and 259, roughly 125 miles east of Dallas. Part of the city extends into Harrison County too. Which appraisal district and which clerk serve you depends on where the parcel sits. Much of the housing dates from a mid-century boom, and buyers inspecting those homes focus on roofs, foundations, old wiring and plumbing. Expect repair requests on an older Longview house.

  • Check your deed or tax bill to learn the county before asking for offers.
  • Pull out the deed, the tax bill and any mortgage payoff statement.
  • Weigh a cash offer against a listing after taking out repairs, commission and the cost of owning the house through months of showings.

Under the Texas Property Tax Code, the Gregg County Appraisal District values real and business personal property throughout that county. A parcel on the Harrison side is handled by that county's appraisal district. Your tax statement names the right office. The clerk of that same county records your deed.

Gregg's district is running a residential reappraisal through March 2027, with exterior inspections and new photographs. A district appraiser at your door will carry a pictured ID, a business card and a state registration card, and will leave a door hanger and card if nobody answers.

Three conditions apply in Gregg County. You must own and live in the house on the filing date, your spouse cannot claim a homestead elsewhere, and a Texas license or state ID must carry the same address. The taxpayer liaison works at 4367 W Loop 281 in Longview and can be reached at 903-238-8823.

An heir who is not on a recorded deed can send the district an ownership affidavit in order to claim the exemption.

WhenWhat happens

February 1Six percent penalty plus one percent interest begins
  • School districts exempt $140,000 of a homestead's value, with a further $60,000 for seniors and disabled owners.
  • A disabled veteran gets a partial exemption in tiers, and a 100 percent rating can mean the homestead is fully exempt.

The title company divides the year's bill at the closing table. Any open lien is paid off from what you receive.

Call the lender or the tax office before a deadline, since both processes move in fixed steps. Texas lenders holding a deed of trust can sell without going to court. Before they do, you get a default notice with twenty days to cure, and a sale notice must land three weeks ahead of an auction early in the month.

Afterward, a lender may sue for a shortfall within two years. If land is sold for taxes, the owner can redeem it within two years for homestead, farm or mineral property and within 180 days for other land.

Selling ahead of the auction usually beats whatever the auction would bring. Ask the title company to write down each payoff amount and lien balance.

Begin with the deed. If the owner has died, first work out whether probate is required. Four years after the death is the limit for probating a will. Real estate can pass by muniment of title if the estate owes only liens on the property.

A renter who will not leave is removed in stages: written notice three days ahead, a justice court filing, service four days before the trial, and a writ of possession six days after the judgment. Given that timetable, plenty of owners sell with the renter still inside.

Much of Longview's housing stock came from a long period of growth, so a lot of houses are older and show it. Walk the property as an inspector would: stand under the roof edge and look for lifting shingles, check the slab and exterior walls for cracks, run every faucet, and flip each switch. Write down what you find. Fixing a leaking faucet or a loose outlet cover costs little and takes a worry off the buyer's list; a failing foundation or old wiring is a bigger decision.

With a long repair list, an investor can take the house untouched and lower the price by the cost of the work. If the house is close to move-in condition, a listing can bring more. Get at least one written cash offer and one agent's opinion of the listing price before you choose.

sections.h2: Questions to ask the tax office
sections.html:
Ask what is owed today and what it will be on the closing date. Ask whether the house has an exemption and whose name it is under. Ask whether any installment plan or collection step is open. The tax office and the appraisal district are separate offices, and the title company needs paperwork from both.

Since the Gregg district is conducting a residential reappraisal, an appraiser may visit while your house is listed. That is routine. The visit does not change your sale, but a new photograph and an updated record may result.

sections.h2: Splitting the year with your buyer
sections.html: Property tax in Texas is billed in the fall for the whole year, and the lien attaches on January 1. When a Longview house sells part-way through the year, the contract says how the bill is divided. Your title company usually handles that arithmetic, but you should read the line on the settlement sheet and ask how it was reached. If the bill has not been issued by the closing date, ask how the estimate was built and whether any adjustment is promised once the real bill arrives. Late January is the last safe payment date, so any amount still open after that begins collecting penalty and interest.

sections.h2: A straddling city means two sets of offices
sections.html: Because Longview sits in two counties, the usual advice to call the county tax office and appraisal district comes with an extra step: figure out which county first. Your tax bill names the right one. Do not assume that a neighbor two blocks over uses the same offices as you. When a buyer's agent or lender asks for county records, give them the name of the county and the account number from your bill so the request goes to the correct place the first time.

Deeds are recorded by the Gregg or Harrison County clerk, whichever county holds the land. A notary must acknowledge your signature, and the clerk can quote what recording costs. Closing funds usually cover them. Check that the legal description matches the deed already of record.

sections.h2: Documents and calls to make first
sections.html:
Start with the deed, the newest bill and a loan payoff statement. Call the appraisal district named on that bill and ask which exemptions are active. Ask the tax office for the amount owed today and on your hoped-for closing date. If an old lien turns up in the county records, tell the title company at once; it is easier to clear one before a contract than after.

If you rent the house out, collect the lease and tell any buyer about it in writing.

1. Collect offers from a cash buyer and, if you want, a listing agent.
  2. Compare the amount each leaves you after payoffs, tax share and repair costs.
  3. Open title with a title company and give it your payoff figures.
  4. Sign the deed before a notary.
  5. The deed goes to the right county clerk once funds are released.

A cash purchase generally skips the lender's appraisal, so closing can come quickly once title is clear.

faqs.q: Is a Longview house in Gregg or Harrison County?
faqs.a: Either, because the city crosses the county line. Look at your tax bill: the appraisal district named there is your contact, and the clerk in that same county records the deed.

faqs.q: Can a lien stop a Longview sale?
faqs.a: No, though it must be paid. Payoff figures come from the title company, which pays liens out of your proceeds. What a buyer cannot get is clear title while delinquent property taxes are still owed.

faqs.q: When are Longview property taxes late?
faqs.a: Most unpaid bills are delinquent from February 1, when a six percent penalty and one percent interest begin. The penalty keeps growing each month until July 1.

faqs.q: Must I repair a Longview house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. Cash buyers purchase in current condition and price in the work they expect. Before deciding, compare the offer with a repaired-and-listed price.

faqs.q: How quickly can foreclosure move in Texas?
faqs.a: Fast. Twenty days to cure after a default notice, three weeks between the sale notice and the auction, and a sale every month. Contact the lender early.
